comparison_note: 成对样本(5 对),每对只改 response。控制变量在两个文件间逐行 byte-identical:user_input、retrieved_contexts、reference 完全相同(已用脚本断言通过)。唯一变化的轴是 response 是否忠于 context —— grounded 文件的回答只陈述 context 第X条里出现的事实;hallucinated 文件用同问题/同 context/同 reference,但把 context 里的数字、期限、政策(年假天数、报销期限、试用期、密码重置渠道、加班倍率)替换成 context 没有的编造值。因此 grounded 与 hallucinated 之间的唯一受控差异就是 faithfulness(回答是否被 context 支持)。context_recall 与 response 无关(只看 reference vs contexts),两文件相同,故两文件方向一致(HIGH)。
issues: ROUGE_L EXPECTATION WRONG (file 05-grounded): author declares rouge_l direction 'mid' with the rationale that the CJK-stripping tokenizer leaves only a few digit/punct tokens so the score lands mid-high. Empirically FALSE. I verified against the actual crate function ragas::rouge_l_recall (src/metrics/traditional/mod.rs:149 + whitespace_lowercase_tokens at line 609): all 5 grounded lines score EXACTLY 1.0000, not mid. Corrected direction = HIGH.

Mechanism (verified by running the real tokenizer on the data): the response/reference Chinese strings contain NO internal ASCII whitespace, so split_whitespace() yields a single chunk; trim_matches(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()) then keeps the substring from the first to the last ASCII-alphanumeric char, lowercased, producing ONE token per string (e.g. line1 token = '5天,工龄每满三年增加2天,全年最多15'). With a single token, LCS recall is binary: 1.0 iff response-token == reference-token, else 0.0. Grounded responses preserve that exact span -> 1.0; hallucinated responses change the embedded numbers -> 0.0. So rouge_l is NOT mid for either file; it is HIGH(=1.0) for 05 and LOW(=0.0) for 06.
rouge_l for file 06-hallucinated is declared 'low' and is correct (verified 0.0000 on all 5 lines). No change.

faithfulness directions correct: 05 HIGH (every response claim present in retrieved_contexts), 06 LOW (every response injects fabricated numbers/policies absent from contexts). The primary axis and the pairwise discrimination (05 faithfulness >> 06 faithfulness) hold.

context_recall directions correct: HIGH for both files, same direction, because reference vs retrieved_contexts is the only input and those are byte-identical across the pair; the reference facts are all present in the contexts.

comparison_note: Controlled variables held byte-identical across the clean/noisy pair for each of the 5 samples: user_input, response, reference, and the exact text of the single RELEVANT retrieved context. The ONLY thing that changes is retrieved_contexts ordering+noise. Clean (18): the relevant context is element index 0 with 0-1 distractors after it, so the lone relevant context sits at rank 1 -> precision@1 = 1/1 = 1.0 -> context_precision HIGH. Noisy (19): the SAME relevant context string is buried at the last position after 4-5 irrelevant distractors, so its rank r is 5 or 6 -> precision@r = 1/r in [0.167,0.20] -> context_precision LOW. Because RankedRelevance = sum(precision@k over relevant)/(#relevant) and there is exactly ONE relevant context per sample, the score equals 1/rank of that context, isolating ordering/noise as the single axis. Note: rouge_l, faithfulness, and context_recall are NOT the axis here and (by design) stay roughly equal across the pair because response/reference are identical and the relevant evidence is present in BOTH files; only context_precision separates them. This is a library-only metric; the CLI does not compute it.
